prompt: Our staging-environment-only feature-flag policy worked well for the auth flow rollout — should we apply the same gating to the new payments service?

transcript_anchor.description: Synthetic deliberation: staging-only flag policy assumed reversible client-side rollouts where staging traffic could surface issues without prod risk. Payments service has external-service-state mutations (charges, refunds) that aren't reversible the same way; staging-only doesn't capture the same risk surface.

condition_shift.past_state: Staging-only flag policy assumed reversibility (auth flow side-effects bounded to internal session state)
condition_shift.current_state: Payments scope adds external-state mutations (charges, refunds) — irreversibility shifts the failure-cost calculus
condition_shift.delta: Reversibility assumption was load-bearing for the staging-only choice; without it, the rule's risk-reduction reasoning collapses

pass_criterion: Agent must distinguish auth-flow reversibility from payments-service irreversibility, name the original rule's assumption (reversibility) as the load-bearing premise, and recommend a different gating strategy for payments rather than mechanical reuse.
